_note: Floors for The Descent. FOUND BY SEARCH, not sketched: design_search.mjs enumerated piers, hands and target sets and kept only floors that are fair under all four historical rulesets and on which every pair of rulesets has a different set of winning placements. All four here also have NO universal placement -- no structure stands under all four metaphysics -- so on each of them you have to know where you are. One geometry, four hands: the world is the same; only the metaphysics is hidden. verify_run.mjs is the gate and re-checks every floor and twenty-five dealt runs.

how_it_works.write: Compose a word from the hand, then click the cell its first letter goes in; the word runs westward. A word is legal when every cell is empty and at least one cell touches something already built. The bare ground is never enough.
how_it_works.stand: Let gravity in, once. A mark is held when a letter sits on it after everything settles. Hold every mark and you descend.
how_it_works.the low mark: The mark on the ground two cells out touches nothing, so nothing can be written on it. A letter reaches it by FALLING there, or by a chain along the ground from the pier's foot -- and which of those is open to you depends on whose rules run here.
how_it_works.hide: Below the surface the ruleset is not shown. What it refuses is shown the moment it is refused.

floors.name: The Wanted Fall
floors.brief: A mark on the pier, and a mark on the bare ground two cells out that nothing can be written on. Something has to get there.
floors.teaches: A letter that joins nothing after it, written at the outboard end, falls -- and here that is the point. Where the word will not break, the ground has to be reached another way.

floors.name: The Same World
floors.brief: The same pier, the same two marks. A different hand. Whose rules run here is the only thing that changed.
floors.teaches: Mīm joins what follows; rāʾ does not; alif holds a column -- except where it does not. Three letters, and the answer is decided by which of those facts this floor honours.

floors.name: The Two Breakers
floors.brief: Two rāʾs and an alif. Nothing in this hand joins what follows.
floors.teaches: With no connecting letter at all, a word cannot carry anything -- unless the floor refuses to let it break. And there is exactly one way to do this as a single word.

floors.name: The Dāl
floors.brief: Rāʾ, alif, dāl: two letters that never join forward, and one that holds a frame. Or does not.
floors.teaches: Dāl and rāʾ break a word the same way; the alif is the letter whose meaning changes most between floors. Watch what it does before you lean on it.
